entries.title: Fixed ellipticity permits arbitrarily small positive speeds
entries.statement: DRAFT audit material; independent review pending. Fix d>=2, b=1/(2d), kappa=1/(4d), and 0<epsilon<=kappa. At every site take probabilities b+epsilon for +e1, b-epsilon for -e1 and b in every other direction. This deterministic product environment is site iid and UE with the fixed bound kappa. Its walk has velocity 2epsilon e1 and E T_1=1/(2epsilon), where T_1 is first arrival at projected height one. Thus a law-independent positive speed lower bound or finite crossing-mean upper bound depending only on d,kappa is impossible.
assumptions: Not a proof or refutation of C0041

entries.title: Invalid uniform speed bridge
entries.statement: DRAFT audit material; independent review pending. The auxiliary assertion that there exists c(d,kappa)>0 such that every directionally transient site-iid UE nearest-neighbor law on Z^d has directional speed at least c(d,kappa) is false. The homogeneous epsilon family at fixed kappa=1/(4d) has speed 2epsilon decreasing to zero. The qualitative C0041 implication for each individual law is a distinct assertion.
assumptions: Not a proof or refutation of C0041

entries.title: Critical two-point crossing mean
entries.statement: DRAFT audit material; independent review pending. In dimension one let site right-jump probabilities be iid, equal to 3/4 with probability 3/4 and 1/4 otherwise. The walk is UE, transient to the right, and has zero speed. For rho=(1-p)/p, E log rho=-(log3)/2 and E rho=1. The first crossing expectation has lower bound E T_1>=2L+1 for every integer L>=1, hence is infinite. A geometric-excursion recursion yields the bound; a stationary ergodic argument with truncated, generally dependent crossing durations gives zero speed. Dimension one is outside C0041.
assumptions: Not a proof or refutation of C0041

entries.title: Layered lift loses site independence
entries.statement: DRAFT audit material; independent review pending. For d>=2 let p_i be the critical iid sequence from the preceding construction and define omega(x,+e1)=p_x1/2, omega(x,-e1)=(1-p_x1)/2, and omega(x,+/-ej)=1/[4(d-1)] for j>=2. This nearest-neighbor environment is stationary and ergodic under the full translation group and UE with lower bound min(1/8,1/[4(d-1)]). The walk is directionally transient in e1 and has zero vector speed despite raw mean local e1 drift 1/8. It is not site iid: two different sites sharing x1 have favorable-type indicator covariance 3/16. An independent Bernoulli axial clock reduces the first coordinate to the one-dimensional example.
assumptions: Not a proof or refutation of C0041

entries.title: Stationary ergodicity does not replace site iid
entries.statement: DRAFT audit material; independent review pending. The stronger auxiliary statement that UE and stationary ergodicity under the full translation group suffice to turn directional transience into positive speed in d>=2 is false. The critical layered law above is transient with zero speed. Shared layer variables violate site independence, so this is not a counterexample to C0041's iid-site statement.
assumptions: Not a proof or refutation of C0041

entries.title: Directional regeneration integrability audit boundary
entries.statement: DRAFT audit material; independent review pending. A directional-transience proof must distinguish finite regeneration times almost surely from finite conditional mean duration E0[tau_1|D=infinity], where D is first backtracking below the starting height. The classical renewal formula gives positive directional speed when that mean is finite. C0041's precise site-iid UE d>=2 implication has a September-23-2026 public resolution claim, not independently validated in this packet; its decisive small-quenched-crossing-probability estimate is the next mathematical proof gate. Source status is UNKNOWN, not certified open.
assumptions: Not a proof or refutation of C0041

relations.rationale: The explicit product point-mass laws keep d,kappa fixed while their speed tends to zero.
The axial coordinate at Bernoulli clock times is the critical one-dimensional walk.
The full-group ergodic UE construction escapes directionally with zero speed and has covariance 3/16 across same-layer sites.
The family satisfies the target's exact hypotheses and restricts any attempted quantitative speed constant.
The target conclusion fails after site iid is replaced by full-group stationary ergodicity; the missing premise is explicit.
The original target and the new public claim share the regeneration-duration proof gate.
